rounds.text: The market is severely punishing Prevest Denpro Ltd, reflecting profound structural or sentiment exhaustion that goes beyond mere valuation metrics. Compounded share price growth sits at -11% over 3 years and -29% over 1 year [E20, E21], with the twelve-month price return plunging -34.3% [E47] and the stock lingering deep down near 18% to 26% of its 52-week range [E5, E43]. Technical health is decidedly broken: the stock trades below its 200-day moving average [E45, E62], boasts a dismal relative-strength rating of just 10 against the Nifty 500 [E46, E61], and exhibits an annualized volatility of 54.0% [E49]. Compounding this downward pressure, the rules-based screen flags decelerating earnings growth [E60] alongside an "Inconsistent" yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E27, E28], punctuated by a margin contraction from 40% down to 36% over a three-year span [E25]. Furthermore, the valuation is not uniformly cheap, as the EV/EBITDA of 13.3x and price-to-book ratio of 3.76x both command a premium over their respective sector benchmarks of 10.65x and 3.13x [E7, E11].
